title: Smooth locality on source-and-target for algebraic-space morphisms
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal P$ be a property of morphisms of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Smoothness is the compatible etale scheme-chart test [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] for smooth scheme morphisms [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. The point classes $|X|$ identify field-valued maps after common field extensions [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes], and images of maps on point classes use [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Say that $\mathcal P$ is smooth local on source-and-target if: (i) for every smooth $a:U\to X$ and every $r:X\to Y$ with $\mathcal P(r)$, the composite $ra$ has $\mathcal P$; (ii) in every algebraic-space pullback square [def-pc-fibre-product] above $r:X\to Y$, smoothness of $b:Y^{\prime}\to Y$ and $\mathcal P(r)$ imply $\mathcal P(X\times_Y Y^{\prime}\to Y^{\prime})$; (iii) for every $r:X\to Y$, $\mathcal P(r)$ holds if and only if for every $x\in|X|$ there exist algebraic spaces $U,V$, smooth maps $a:U\to X$, $b:V\to Y$, a map $h:U\to V$ with $ra=bh$, and $u\in|U|$ with $a(u)=x$, such that $\mathcal P(h)$.
